rules.statement: The final (production) stage of a host container image sets `Logging__Console__FormatterName=json`, `Logging__Console__FormatterOptions__UseUtcTimestamp=true` and `Logging__Console__FormatterOptions__TimestampFormat=O`, so every log entry is one JSON object on one line with a UTC round-trip timestamp.
rules.why: A container log collector reads standard output one line at a time. The multi-line `simple` format splits one entry into several records and separates an exception from the entry that reports it. UTC timestamps let entries from replicas in different time zones sort together.
rules.check: Look for a Dockerfile final stage that is missing any of the three environment variables, sets a different formatter, or drops UTC or the `O` timestamp format.

rules.statement: Set the default log output format in the container image itself, not in a Helm chart or other deployment manifest, and leave operators to override it through environment variables.
rules.why: The same image run with `docker run` or on another orchestrator would otherwise write a different format, and the artifact that is shipped would differ from the one that is run.
rules.check: Look for Helm values or chart templates that add their own `Logging__Console__*` defaults instead of leaving them to the image and to operator-supplied `extraEnv`.

rules.statement: Keep the human-readable `simple` console formatter for debug or development image stages and local runs (`dotnet run`, AppHost), and select the JSON formatter only in the production image stage.
rules.why: Debug stages and local runs write to a console that a person reads, and JSON is harder to read by eye.
rules.check: Look for the JSON formatter forced in a `base` or debug Dockerfile stage, in launchSettings, or in appsettings that local runs load.

rules.statement: Every process that runs from the same image, such as a migration worker, registers the console logging provider the same way the host does, so it reads the same `Logging:Console` configuration.
rules.why: Then all processes in the image write the same one-line JSON format that the collector expects.
rules.check: Look for a worker or tool entry point in the image that sets up console logging differently, for example by hard-coding a formatter or skipping configuration binding.

rules.statement: A library package never chooses its host's logging sinks or output formatter.
rules.why: The output format is part of the sink, and choosing the sink belongs to the host, not to a library.
rules.check: Look for library extension methods that call `AddConsole`, `AddJsonConsole` or `AddSimpleConsole`, set `FormatterName`, or add other logging providers.
